urgent.heading: Urgent — call now
urgent.primary_message: Call an ambulance immediately. Note the exact time symptoms started.
red_flags: One side of the face drooping — ask them to smile
Arm weakness on one side — ask them to raise both arms
Speech slurred or strange — ask them to repeat a sentence
Sudden severe headache with no known cause
Sudden vision loss in one or both eyes

what_is_it.heading: Stroke in plain terms
what_is_it.lede: A stroke happens when blood flow to part of the brain is suddenly cut off. Brain cells start dying within minutes.
paragraphs: Most strokes happen when a clot blocks a blood vessel in the brain. A smaller number happen when a vessel bursts and blood leaks in. Both are emergencies and look the same from the outside — you cannot tell which is which without a hospital scan.
The faster a stroke is treated, the more of the brain can be saved. Clot-busting medicines work best within the first few hours. After that, the damage becomes permanent. This is why minutes matter.

items.headline: Minutes matter
items.body: Around 2 million brain cells die every minute during a stroke. The clock starts at the first symptom.
South Africans have a stroke every year. It is a leading cause of adult disability and death.

items.headline: Preventable
items.body: Most strokes are linked to high blood pressure, smoking, diabetes, and diet — all of which can be managed.

items.headline: Recovery is possible
items.body: Acting in the first hour gives the best chance of full recovery. Hospitals have time-sensitive treatments.

pull_quote.text: If you suspect a stroke, do not wait to see how it goes. Call an ambulance. Even if symptoms pass on their own — that itself is a warning sign.

signs.heading: The FAST test
signs.lede: Stroke symptoms come on suddenly. The faster you recognise them, the more of the brain can be saved. Remember FAST.

items.title: F — Face drooping
items.description: Ask them to smile. Does one side of the mouth or face droop, even subtly?

items.title: A — Arm weakness
items.description: Ask them to raise both arms. Does one drift downward or feel numb? Can they hold both up equally?

items.title: S — Speech difficulty
items.description: Ask them to repeat a simple sentence. Is their speech slurred, strange, or hard to understand?

items.title: T — Time to call
items.description: If you see any of these signs, call 10177 right away. Note the exact time symptoms started.

myths.heading: What is true and what is not

items.myth: Strokes only happen to older people.
items.fact: Strokes can happen at any age. About 1 in 4 strokes happens in people under 65, and the number is rising in young adults.

items.myth: If the symptoms pass quickly, it wasn't a real stroke.
items.fact: A brief episode (a TIA or 'mini-stroke') is a serious warning. About 1 in 3 people who have a TIA will have a full stroke — many within 48 hours.

items.myth: I should drive them to hospital myself — faster than waiting for an ambulance.
items.fact: Paramedics start treatment in the ambulance and route to the right stroke-capable hospital. Driving yourself wastes critical time and is dangerous.

items.myth: Aspirin will help during a stroke.
items.fact: Do not give aspirin during a suspected stroke. If it is a bleeding stroke (about 1 in 5 cases), aspirin will make it worse. Call the ambulance and wait.

action_steps.heading: What to do — the moment you suspect a stroke

items.title: Call 10177 or 112 immediately
items.description: Say the word 'stroke' clearly. Paramedics will prioritise and route to a stroke-capable hospital.

items.title: Note the exact time symptoms started
items.description: This determines which treatments are possible. Even an approximate time helps the hospital team.

items.title: Do not give food, water, or medication
items.description: The person may have trouble swallowing. Do not give anything by mouth — including aspirin.

items.title: If unconscious, lay them on their side
items.description: The recovery position keeps the airway clear. If conscious, keep them comfortable and reassured.

items.title: Stay with them until paramedics arrive
items.description: Watch their breathing. Be ready to perform CPR if they stop breathing. Unlock the door so paramedics can enter.

get_help.heading: Who to call right now
get_help.lede: A suspected stroke is an emergency. Call now. Do not drive yourself or wait for symptoms to pass on their own.
